findings.title: The two-machine procedure still pins the Net-3e SIM 35 candidate and revision, so its new guest command cannot run as written
findings.claim: The diff updates only the guest command (L21) and the coordination paragraph (L24). The preparation section still says to use the Net-3e candidate, check out its revision and overlay its driver-source archive. At that revision the smoke has no `--join-code-file` argument. Its manifest reads `sim: 35`. So an owner who follows the document gets `arguments-invalid` on the guest, and any report fails the SIM 39 identity schema.
findings.evidence: docs/superpowers/prompts/2026-11-15-net-3e-two-machine-playtest.md:L13 ("Use `final-fix-evidence/candidate.json` and a checkout of its revision `65b92a3d…`", overlay `dist/net-3e-final-driver-source.zip`, "all265 entries"), L3 (status links to the Net-3e release candidate), L34 (the 'Ordinary internet' row still says Host/Join/Ready/Start and pause/resume, but the menu's Host now makes only a duel room). New flag: scripts/network/internet-app-smoke.ts:L329 and L338 (the `allowed` list gains `--join-code-file`). Identity: scripts/network/internet-app-report.ts:L189 (`sim:z.literal(SIM_VERSION)`). Plan L889 sends the owner to this prompt 'as Task 3 Step 1 updates it'.
findings.why: The two-machine runs are owner-only. Run as written, the steps fail, or they test the wrong bytes. Severity rule: 'an owner-only step that cannot be run as written'.
findings.fix: Replace L13 with the H-2b candidate: `dist/h2b-candidate/candidate.json`, its `identity.revision`, and `dist/h2b-candidate.zip`. Either drop the overlay archive or say how to make an H-2b one. Point L3 at the H-2b-ii gates subsection. Rewrite the 'Ordinary internet' row as the two-part duel-then-sector run, matching L24.

findings.title: The owner-only steps in gates.md refer to 'the same command' but never give one
findings.claim: The H-2b-ii subsection lists the owner's deployed and forced-relay runs as 'the same command without `--local-verification`' and 'again with `--force-relay`'. Neither gates.md nor the subsection gives that command, the playtest-report command for the duel records, or the build and package commands. It also does not say to use a new `--report-path` for each run. Rerunning with the same path deletes the earlier run's copied duel records.
findings.evidence: docs/gates.md:L791-L795 ("the same command without `--local-verification`"), L780 (the candidate's build, package and manifest are described in prose only). The exact commands exist only in plan L848, L854 and L888, which also says 'Use new `--report-path` values'. The smoke deletes the copies folder: scripts/network/internet-app-smoke.ts:L436 and L472 (`rmSync(copies,{recursive:true,force:true})`).
findings.why: The gates file is the owner's runbook. Owner-only steps should be exact and runnable in PowerShell 5.1 without opening the plan.
findings.fix: In the subsection, paste the plan's PowerShell block (L824-L834), the manifest command (L843), the local-verification command (L848) and its playtest-report command (L854). Then paste the two deployed commands in full, each with its own `--report-path` (for example `out/h2b-internet/deployed.json` and `out/h2b-internet/relay.json`).

findings.title: A join-code file saved with PowerShell 5.1's `>` or Out-File is UTF-16 and is never accepted
findings.claim: `readCode` decodes the file as UTF-8 and accepts only `/^[0-9A-Z]{8}$/`. In Windows PowerShell 5.1, `'CODE' > file` and `Out-File` write UTF-16LE with a BOM. That decodes to replacement characters and NULs, so the guest polls for 90 s and fails with `driver-timeout`. The procedure gives no way to save the file. The code is also not normalised for the Crockford look-alikes the alphabet leaves out (O, I, L), which an operator can misread off the screen.
findings.evidence: scripts/network/internet-app-smoke.ts:L446 (`readFileSync(codeFile,'utf8').trim().toUpperCase().replace(/^ROOM\s+/,'')`, regex `^[0-9A-Z]{8}$`, `CODE_WAIT_MS` 90000 at L321). docs/superpowers/prompts/2026-11-15-net-3e-two-machine-playtest.md:L24 ('saves it in `PATH/join-code.txt`', no command given). The alphabet is at src/shared/roomSession.ts:L93 (`[0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ]{8}`).
findings.why: The most natural PowerShell 5.1 way to write the file makes the guest's run fail spuriously after a 90 s wait.
findings.fix: Document the exact command: `Set-Content -Path PATH\join-code.txt -Value ABCD1234 -Encoding ASCII`. Also, or instead, make `readCode` decode a UTF-16LE BOM (check for `FF FE` and use `'utf16le'`), and map O→0 and I/L→1 before the regex.

findings.title: The documented steps never produce the SIM 39 localRecovery evidence that internetReady needs
findings.claim: `internetReady` needs the first four gates to PASS, `localRecovery` included. That gate needs a recovery report whose `source.digest` and executable artifacts equal the new candidate's. The only recovery evidence in the repo is Net-3e's, built from the SIM 35 bytes. Neither the gates subsection nor the plan's owner list says to rerun the local recovery smoke on the H-2b candidate.
findings.evidence: scripts/network/internet-app-report.ts:L121-L128 (`source.digest!==base.identity.digest||!same(expected,observed)`) and L133 (`internetReady` needs `statuses.slice(0,4)` all PASS). docs/gates.md:L791-L795 and plan L60-L62 and L885-L891 list no recovery run. The only fixture is the Net-3e `recovery-skiff.json` (tests/internetAppReport.test.ts:L3).
findings.why: Once the owner has done every listed step, the combined readiness report still cannot validate with internetReady true.
findings.fix: Add the recovery smoke on the candidate build to 'Proven before the redeploy' in gates.md, with its command and output path. Also say how its report goes into `localRecovery` (with `runtimeProvenance` if the revisions differ).

findings.title: Several new reject cases do not reach the check they are named for, and the rise checks are untested
findings.claim: 'no beam in the duel' sets `beam.guest=0`. The zod `pos` rule rejects that before `checkDuel`'s `beam.guest<=beam.before` comparison runs, so the comparison is never exercised. No case covers the thrust rise (`thrust.host/guest<=before+1`), the device thrust peak, or the device beam. 'a duel candidate field' is rejected by the key scan (`candidates?`) before the strict schema sees the extra key.
findings.evidence: tests/internetAppReport.test.ts, diff L631 (`beam.guest=0`) and L635 (`candidate='host'`). scripts/network/internet-app-report.ts:L203 (`beam:…host:pos,guest:pos`), L234 (the semantic rise checks), L241 (device `thrust.peak`, `beam.after`) and L91 (the key scan regex includes `candidates?`).
findings.why: Brief item 5 asks for each reject case to hit a distinct check. As written, deleting the semantic rise checks in checkDuel and checkDeviceDuel would leave every test green.
findings.fix: Use `beam.before=1` with `beam.guest=1` for the beam case. Add `thrust.guest=thrust.before+1` (local pair), `deviceDuel.thrust.peak=0.5` and `deviceDuel.beam.after=deviceDuel.beam.before` (with before ≥ 1) cases. Name the extra-field case with a key the scan does not catch, for example `extra`.

findings.title: Triage (a) and (b): the seed comparison relies on parseRun; the manifest message and the plan's artifact count are out of date
findings.claim: (a) `a.deviceDuel?.seed!==b.deviceDuel?.seed` would pass if both were undefined. It is safe today only because `checkDeviceDuel` (called from parseRun) rejects a single-device run without `deviceDuel`. (b) The manifest still prints 'exact out bytes', although it now hashes only three folders. The plan still expects 47 artifacts; the brief reports 50.
findings.evidence: scripts/network/internet-app-report.ts:L109 and L240 (`if(!d||r.duel)fail()`). scripts/network/candidate-manifest.ts:L170 and L160. Plan L844 ('47 artifacts').
findings.why: A later refactor of parseRun could silently let a two-machine bundle with no duel evidence through, and the stale message and count mislead the owner.
findings.fix: Write `!a.deviceDuel||!b.deviceDuel||a.deviceDuel.seed!==b.deviceDuel.seed`. Print 'exact out/main, out/preload and out/renderer bytes' and update plan L844 to match. Drop the fixed artifact count or correct it.

findings.title: Triage (c): a join-code file left behind by a failed run blocks the next run with only a generic message
findings.claim: If the guest fails after its operator saved a code but before `readCode` ran, the file stays on disk. The next guest run then refuses at argument parsing because the file exists, and prints only `internet-driver-arguments-or-report-failed`, with no report.
findings.evidence: scripts/network/internet-app-smoke.ts:L338 (`codeFile&&existsSync(codeFile)` throws `arguments-invalid`), L447 (deletes the file only after a successful read), L545 (the generic catch message). The finally block (L209-L221) never touches `codeFile`.
findings.why: No secret leaks: the operator wrote the file, and room codes are short-lived. But a rerun is confusing, and a stale code stays on disk.
findings.fix: In the finally block, call `if(codeFile)rmSync(codeFile,{force:true})`. Or state in the prompt (L24) that the file must be deleted before a rerun.

findings.title: Triage (e): the `until` predicates dereference the latest publication without null guards
findings.claim: `both()` returns `latest()`, which can be undefined. The `fast`, `fired` and `agreement` predicates read `a.speed`, `a.shots` and `observations.at(-1).publications` directly. A TypeError thrown inside `accept` escapes `until` at once instead of being retried.
findings.why: This fails closed (native-gameplay-failed), so no gate passes wrongly. A transiently empty observation would still fail the run instead of retrying.
findings.fix: Use optional chaining in the predicates (`a?.speed>before+1&&b?.speed>before+1`, `v.observations.at(-1)?.publications??[]`).

Decision 2: electron-builder.yml:L7-L9 packs out/main, out/preload and out/renderer, and the manifest hashes the same three folders (candidate-manifest.ts:L160). electron.vite.config.ts:L13, L16 and L25 put every main, utility, preload and renderer entry into those default folders, so nothing the app loads at runtime is dropped. extraResources is unchanged.

Decision 3, the duel pair: it gets its own `directory/duel` and its own duel observer (smoke L415-L416, observer worker L555-L558, online-observer-build.ts:L575-L579); kinds are duel-host/duel-guest (L324), and the sector cleanup lookup by `kind===peer.role` is unchanged (L534). FTLITE_DUEL_TEST_SEED=2277 is set for duel apps and FTLITE_SECTOR_ONLINE_TEST=1 for sector apps, each removing the other (L374-L375). X then E after an applied result (L407-L408), Return (L425), W for 2 s and Space for 4.5 s (L428, L431), rise on both screens and a common publication hash (L429-L434), sampled round-0 records copied to `<report>-duel-records/{host,guest}` (L435-L437), then shutdown with cleanup recorded (L438-L441).

Decision 3, the sector pair and two machines: the sector pair uses host-sector/join-sector (L514-L515). In the manual path `--join-code-file` is required for the guest, refused for the host and must not exist at start (L338). The capture is 30-180 s from the sector run's start (L342, L508). Decision 4: checkDuel and checkDeviceDuel (internet-app-report.ts:L230-L243) require `duel` xor `deviceDuel` by mode, the own-seat record, held+command>0, host loopback, a guest RTT reading lan/internet (internet under forceRelay), rise checks and balanced cleanup. Duel pids join the uniqueness set (L248-L249). Two-machine seeds must match (L109).

No secrets reach stdout, logs or reports. The room code stays in memory and is passed to the driver over IPC (L420, L459, L503). The driver logs only command names (online-app-smoke.cjs:L251-L255), and child stdout and stderr are discarded (smoke L352, L377). The copied playtest records hold no code, address or candidate (src/renderer/src/net/duelRecord.ts:L13-L17, L35-L39). A grep of out/h2b-internet/ for joinCode, code, address, candidate and token found nothing.

Forced relay reaches the duel apps as well: launch passes `--internet-force-relay` for every kind (smoke L378), and the driver applies it to the hidden transport window (online-app-smoke.cjs:L135). Any relay pair is labelled 'internet' (src/network/rtc/route.ts:L27), so the guest-internet-under-relay rule is reachable.

Triage (d) resolved: the local verification run took elapsedMs 53971 of a 180000 budget, duel half included (out/h2b-internet/local.json:L85-L86). Its duel records read host loopback and guest lan (L4618 and L4626).
